title: Cancellation of a Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan by the Tenant
content:
**1. Who cancels.** Only the tenant can cancel protection under the Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan, and the tenant's request is recorded as a cancellation request.

**2. Active plans.** Because every rental must stay covered, cancellation of an active plan requires a received cancellation request naming the tenant's own insurer and policy number. The insurer requirement applies where the level requires proof of the tenant's own insurance to cancel.

**3. Plans not yet in effect.** A plan in pending effective status may be cancelled without naming an insurer, since its rental is then switched to own insurance or re-enrolled before move-in.

**4. Effective date and fees.** Cancellation takes effect on the covered rental's next billing date, so the current period's fee is kept and not prorated, except that a request made within the free-look period refunds every fee collected.

**5. Coverage source.** On cancellation the covered rental's coverage source becomes the tenant's own insurance.

**6. Open claims.** A plan with an open claim may still be cancelled; the claim is settled on the coverage in force on its loss date.

## What the records must show (active plan)

The cancellation request on file for the plan must be in received status and must carry the tenant's own insurer and policy number. A statement on a call is not a substitute for a received request on the plan's records.

## Condition — result

| Plan status | Insurer and policy number on a received request | Cancellation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| active | present | may be cancelled; effective the next billing date |
| active | absent | not cancelled |
| pending effective | not required | may be cancelled |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A tenant with an active plan sends a received cancellation request naming their renter's insurer and policy number mid-period, outside the free-look period. The cancellation takes effect on the next billing date; the fee for the current period is kept in full; the rental's coverage source becomes own insurance.
